target_objects: stepfunctions state machine ow-tp-<ns>-chain (replaces run_all.sh sleep-600 orchestration)
golden_baseline_location: parent session, /home/ubuntu/tp-aws-golden/reports/ (md5 finance_billing_20260115.csv == .xls == 300862b738fdb8b6add8d1007362c0e0); recorded via TP_FAKETIME='2026-01-15 00:00:00' deterministic legacy run

acceptance_checks.description: reports/finance_billing_<report_date>.csv byte-identical to golden: header Currency,RecordType,RecordCount,TotalAmount; totals per ccy|rectype from all parsed/CUSTBILL*.psv; keys sorted with LC_ALL=C semantics (empty/pipe key sorts last as ',UNKNOWN(),1,0.00'); %d count and %.2f total formatting; rt 01->INVOICE, 02->CREDIT, else UNKNOWN(<rt>); rows with empty first field skipped.
.xls is a byte-identical copy of the .csv (the 2004 'conversion'), preserved for parity.
Report date comes from the state-machine input (report_date), never from wall clock, so golden comparison is deterministic; no embedded timestamps anywhere in artifact bytes.

ow-tp-<ns>-chain runs the report per batch on explicit start with {ns, report_date}: verifies parsed inputs exist (no sleep-600 dependency guessing), invokes the report Lambda, fails visibly on error (no 2>/dev/null || true).
Re-executing the state machine with the same input rewrites identical report bytes; no duplicate or drifting output.
With zero parsed/*.psv objects the execution still succeeds and writes a header-only report (legacy exits 0 with header-only CSV).

Role ow-tp-<ns>-report-role: read on parsed/*, write on reports/* only; state-machine role may invoke only ow-tp-<ns>-report; trust conditioned on source account. No sendmail replacement in scope (legacy delivery is a silent no-op; replacement is out of scope and must be listed as an unverified path if claimed).

encoding_policy.input_encoding: binary .psv as written by the parser (may contain non-UTF-8 bytes in name fields)
encoding_policy.byte_transparency: full: split on the pipe byte without a UTF-8 decode layer; only fields 1 (cust), 4 (amt), 5 (ccy), 6 (rt) are interpreted
encoding_policy.invalid_bytes: never raise; non-UTF-8 name bytes are irrelevant to aggregation and must not fail the run

malformed_record_policy.details: Match perl split semantics: extra pipe-delimited fields beyond 6 are silently dropped; empty amt coerces to 0 (+= on non-numeric string is numeric 0); empty ccy/rt attribute to the ',UNKNOWN()' bucket, present in the golden report. Never fail open.

empty_input_semantics.details: Header-only CSV (and identical .xls) written; execution succeeds.

planted_anomalies.reason: Report never inspects the date field (field 3); detection is the parser's, and the misdated row still aggregates into its ccy|rt bucket per golden bytes.
Name bytes are never decoded or used in aggregation; parser detects.

planted_anomalies.description: The short record surfaces in the report as the ',UNKNOWN(),1,0.00' row — its presence in the golden bytes is the report-level assertion for this anomaly.

planted_anomalies.reason: Trailer records are stripped by the parser and never reach the report; parser detects and ledgers it.
